verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev ships major SDK versions (v3, v4) and documents an end-of-life notice saying 4.5.0 is the last version that supports v3 tasks, with guidance to stay or migrate. The changelog also notes deprecation warnings. That is evidence of versioning with some deprecation handling, but not of a formal, published deprecation policy covering API versions, timelines, or guarantees. A community report calls the v3→v4 transition rushed with stale docs; this does not contradict that versioning exists. Missing for 10: a documented formal deprecation policy (notice periods, support windows), explicit versioning of the HTTP/management API rather than only SDK major versions, and independent corroboration of smooth version transitions.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: v3 is end of life. Trigger.dev 4.5.0 is the last version we officially support for running v3 (SDK v3) tasks. If you still have v3 tasks, stay on 4.5.0 or migrate to v4
